title: AutoCAD vs AutoCAD LT: Which Should You Buy in 2026?
excerpt: AutoCAD LT suits 2D drafting; full AutoCAD adds 3D, seven industry toolsets and automation. Learn which to buy, with India pricing and licensing notes.
body:
Buy AutoCAD LT if your work is 2D drafting and documentation. Buy full AutoCAD if you need 3D modelling, the seven industry toolsets (Architecture, Mechanical, Electrical, MEP, Map 3D, Plant 3D and Raster Design) or customisation and automation. Both are sold by TechZoid as annual subscriptions, and the price gap between them is large enough that choosing correctly matters.

## The short version

AutoCAD LT is the lighter, lower-priced edition built around 2D CAD: lines, geometry, annotation, dimensions, layouts and plotting. AutoCAD is the full product. It does everything LT does, then adds 3D modelling and visualisation, the industry toolsets that come with the subscription, and ways to customise and automate the software.

| | AutoCAD LT | AutoCAD |
|---|---|---|
| Core purpose | 2D drafting, drawing and documentation | 2D drafting plus 3D modelling and specialised design |
| 3D modelling and rendering | Not the focus; 2D only for practical purposes | Included |
| Industry toolsets (Architecture, Mechanical, Electrical, MEP, Map 3D, Plant 3D, Raster Design) | Not included | All seven included |
| Customisation and automation | Limited | Supported |
| Web and mobile apps | Check current entitlement | Included with the subscription |
| Licensing | Named user, annual | Named user, annual |
| Price per user per year, excl. GST | {{price:autocad-lt}} | {{price:autocad}} |
| Price per user per year, incl. 18% GST | {{gst:autocad-lt}} | {{gst:autocad}} |

Product pages: [AutoCAD LT](/products/autocad-lt) and [AutoCAD](/products/autocad). Prices exclude GST unless stated, and a written quotation fixes the final price.

## What AutoCAD LT is good at

LT covers the daily work of drawing production. If your drawings are plans, sections, elevations, detail sheets, single-line diagrams, layouts for fit-outs or shop-floor sketches, you spend almost all your time in 2D. LT gives you the drawing and annotation tools, DWG files that open with the people you exchange drawings with, layouts and plotting.

Typical LT buyers in India include:

- Interior designers and fit-out contractors producing furniture and ceiling layouts
- Small architecture and civil consultancies whose deliverables are 2D drawing sets
- Electrical and plumbing contractors drawing layouts and schematics
- Fabrication and shop drawing offices where the model lives in someone else's software
- Draughtspeople and estimators who mark up and revise existing DWGs

For these users, paying for features they never open is wasted budget. The catalogue describes LT as cost-effective 2D CAD software for drafting, drawing and documentation, and that is the right way to think about it.

## What full AutoCAD adds

**3D modelling and visualisation.** If you need to build solid or surface models, check clearances in three dimensions, or produce rendered views for a client, you need full AutoCAD. The product includes 3D modelling, visualisation and rendering.

**The seven industry toolsets.** The current AutoCAD subscription includes Architecture, Mechanical, Electrical, MEP, Map 3D, Plant 3D and Raster Design at no additional cost. These were once separate purchases. They add discipline-specific objects and libraries: intelligent walls, doors and windows for architectural drawings, standard mechanical parts, electrical symbols and panel schedules, mapping and GIS-style data for Map 3D, piping and plant layouts for Plant 3D, and tools for cleaning up scanned drawings with Raster Design. If even one of these matches your daily work, full AutoCAD can pay back through time saved.

**Customisation and automation.** Larger teams standardise their output with custom tools, scripts and routines, and full AutoCAD is the edition that supports this. LT is more limited here. A drawing office that wants an in-house toolbar, automated title-block filling or batch plotting scripts should read this row of the table carefully.

**Drawing comparison, sheet sets and shared project files.** The full subscription lists DWG comparison and drawing history, sheet sets and layout management and Autodesk Docs integration among its features. Check the current feature list for LT on Autodesk's published pages before you assume parity here.

**Web and mobile.** The full AutoCAD subscription includes the web and mobile applications, which are useful on site when you want a current drawing on a tablet rather than a printout.

## A decision rule that works

Ask four questions about the person who will hold the seat:

1. Will they build or edit 3D models for client deliverables? If yes, AutoCAD.
2. Do they draw with discipline-specific objects such as architectural walls, piping or electrical panels? If yes, AutoCAD, because the toolsets are included.
3. Does your firm rely on custom tools or automation? If yes, AutoCAD.
4. Is their output a 2D drawing set that someone else models, reviews or builds from? If yes to this and no to the others, LT.

If the answers are mixed across a team, mix the licences. Subscriptions are assigned per named user, so a practice with eight draughtspeople and two senior designers can reasonably hold eight LT seats and two full AutoCAD seats. That is usually better than buying everyone the full product or squeezing everyone into LT.

## Cost: think per seat, then per year

The catalogue price of LT is considerably lower than full AutoCAD, and for a team of ten pure-2D drafters, the difference across a year is large. But do not choose purely on price. The expensive mistake in this decision is buying LT for someone who then needs 3D or an industry toolset three months later. You end up buying a second subscription, and your drawing standards are split across two editions.

The opposite mistake is also common. Firms buy full AutoCAD for everybody because it was simpler to administer, and half the seats never leave the 2D drafting commands. Pull usage data and ask your drafters what they actually use. Our article on [AutoCAD subscription versus the alternatives](/blog/autocad-subscription-versus-the-alternatives) explains how to count real usage, and [AutoCAD subscription price in India](/blog/autocad-subscription-price-in-india) covers the buying decision for the full product.

## Common mistakes when choosing

**Buying by headcount instead of by task.** A studio with twelve drafters rarely has twelve identical needs. One or two people usually do the 3D views or toolset work. List what each person produces in a typical month before you assign editions.

**Forgetting the people who receive drawings.** If your clients send you files built with toolset objects, you may still open and view them in LT, but editing intelligent objects is a different matter. Ask the sender what they used.

**Treating LT as a trial of the full product.** LT is a product in its own right with its own annual subscription. If you suspect you will need the full edition within the year, buy it now rather than paying twice.

**Overlooking the web option.** Some people only need to look at a drawing or make a quick markup on site. A seat of AutoCAD Web may cover that without a desktop edition.

**Ignoring renewal.** At every renewal, look at who actually opened the software. A seat that moved from drafting to project management may no longer need the full edition at all.

## A worked example

Consider a 15-person electrical design consultancy. Ten engineers produce panel layouts, cable routes and single-line diagrams as 2D drawings. Three senior engineers also use electrical symbol libraries and schedules heavily and occasionally model cable trays in 3D. Two project managers open drawings for review a few times a month.

A sensible split is LT for the ten drafting seats, full AutoCAD for the three seniors (the Electrical toolset is included), and either AutoCAD Web or Flex for the two reviewers. This puts the full-edition cost only where it earns its keep, and it keeps everyone on DWG, so files move between them freely. The exact mix will differ in your business, which is why we ask for a role list before quoting.

## Other options in the same family

- **[AutoCAD Web](/products/autocad-web)** is a lower-cost way to draft, annotate and add field data to DWG files in a browser or on a mobile device. It suits site staff and reviewers who do not need a desktop seat. Its price is {{price:autocad-web}} per user per year, excluding GST.
- **[Autodesk Flex](/products/autodesk-flex)** is a token-based option for occasional users. If someone opens AutoCAD only a few days a year, read [Flex versus named-user subscriptions](/blog/autodesk-flex-versus-named-user-subscriptions) before buying a full seat. Flex is priced on enquiry.
- **[AEC Collection](/products/aec-collection)** bundles AutoCAD with Revit, Civil 3D and more. If a person already needs AutoCAD and another Autodesk product, compare the collection before buying two subscriptions. See [the AEC Collection explained](/blog/autodesk-aec-collection-explained).

## Hardware and platform

The AutoCAD catalogue entry lists 64-bit Windows 11 and Windows 10, a macOS release whose feature set differs from the Windows one, 16 GB of RAM as a minimum with 32 GB recommended for large drawings, and a DirectX 12 capable GPU with 4 GB of VRAM or more. LT users working on simple 2D drawings may run lighter, but confirm the current requirements on Autodesk's published pages before you specify hardware. Fast single-thread performance and an SSD matter more than a very expensive graphics card for typical drafting.

## How licensing works

Both editions are licensed per named user. A subscription is assigned to one person and cannot be shared, but it can be reassigned when someone leaves. Each user can sign in on one machine at a time. That means a drawing office with ten people needs ten seats, even if only six are active at any one time, so remove seats you do not use at renewal. More on this in [what changed with Autodesk named-user licensing](/blog/autodesk-named-user-licensing-what-changed).

Note that older sources, including some earlier TechZoid pages, describe LT as folded into the main AutoCAD line. That is not how we currently sell it: AutoCAD LT is its own annual product in our catalogue, and you can order it separately.

## Buying in India

Every order carries a GST invoice at 18%, which a GST-registered business can generally claim as input credit. If you want a single quotation covering a mix of LT and full seats, [send us an enquiry](/enquiry) with the number of users in each role. Monthly and multi-year terms can be quoted on request. For a wider view of the market, see our [CAD software guide](/cad-software).

faqs.question: Is AutoCAD LT enough for architectural drawings?
faqs.answer: For 2D plans, sections, elevations and detail sheets, yes. LT handles drafting, annotation, dimensions, layouts and plotting. If you want the Architecture toolset with intelligent walls, doors and windows, or 3D modelling, you need full AutoCAD, which includes that toolset.

faqs.question: Can AutoCAD LT open and save DWG files from AutoCAD users?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both editions work with DWG files, so you can exchange drawings with consultants and contractors who use full AutoCAD. The practical difference is what you can create and edit inside the drawing, such as 3D solids or toolset objects, rather than whether the file opens.

faqs.question: Does AutoCAD LT include 3D modelling?
faqs.answer: LT is positioned for 2D drafting and documentation. If 3D modelling, visualisation or rendering is part of your deliverables, buy full AutoCAD. If you only occasionally view a 3D model, a lighter route such as a viewer or web workflow may be enough.

faqs.question: Can I upgrade from AutoCAD LT to AutoCAD later?
faqs.answer: You can buy a full AutoCAD subscription for that user when the need arises. Because the products are separate annual subscriptions in our catalogue, ask for a quotation before renewal so the change is planned rather than bought twice.

faqs.question: Are the industry toolsets included with AutoCAD in India?
faqs.answer: Yes. The current AutoCAD subscription includes Architecture, Mechanical, Electrical, MEP, Map 3D, Plant 3D and Raster Design at no extra cost, along with the web and mobile apps. Teams still paying separately for a toolset should review their entitlement.

faqs.question: Can two people share one AutoCAD LT subscription?
faqs.answer: No. Autodesk subscriptions are named-user: one seat is assigned to one person, though it can be reassigned if they leave. For occasional users, consider Autodesk Flex or AutoCAD Web rather than sharing a login.
